DRIFT final campaign: results

Five answer models x seven forgetting policies x three benchmarks, plus RQ4, grace period, matching ablation and held-out weights. Every number is recomputed from saved per-question records.

Overview

Averages over the five answer models. P0 = append-only, P2 = bitemporal contradiction invalidation.

Explorer

Pick a benchmark and a metric. Cells are coloured from worst (light) to best (teal). Click a policy row to plot it across models.

P2 against every other policy

Per question, paired. Interval: paired bootstrap 95%. p: exact McNemar, Holm-corrected within each scope. W/L: questions P2 got right and the other policy wrong, and the reverse.

Who benefits from forgetting

Mean per-question change from P0 to P2, grouped by model tier.

RQ4: several agents, one memory (MQuAKE-T)

Every answering role is Gemini 3.8 Flash so only the memory differs. Shared: five different models write one memory. Independent: each agent keeps its own memory from 80% of the sessions. Orchestrator: one memory, a router picks a specialist.

Grace period with history questions

History accuracy = answering "what was it before the last change". Small models; P2 deletes a closed fact after the grace period.

How contradictions are detected

P2 with exact relation names, normalised names (main run), or an LLM check (as in Zep). Small models.

Retrieval weights on an unseen benchmark

FactConsolidation, P2. The search that chose the alternatives never saw this benchmark.
